# Equal-mass asymmetric outer pairs: no relocated full reflected credit

This is an exact obstruction to extending the FULL collective reflected-pair payment to equal-mass outer pairs merely by relocating the common center. It is an actual complete six-interval body. Every candidate mark, every ambient normal, and both continuous orientations are controlled. It does not contradict the weaker mixed centerpoint target: its depth is well above that target.

## 1. Actual compatible body and the proposed credit

Take continuous dimension d=1 and integer dimension n=1. At integer bases z=-2,-1,0,1,2,3, prescribe

    K_-2=K_3=[-1,-9/10],
    K_-1=K_2=[-1,1/20],
    K_0=K_1=B=[-1,1].                              (1)

Let C be their canonical convex hull. The lower endpoint roof is constant -1. The successive upper-roof slopes are

    19/20, 19/20, 0, -19/20, -19/20.

They are nonincreasing, so C has exactly the fibers (1). Its projection is [-2,3], and those are all its integer fibers. No unmeasured gap or omitted intermediate lattice fiber is involved.

The near outer pair has equal masses a_1=21/20 and the far pair equal masses a_2=1/10. Both members of each pair lie in B. Set

    b=2,    S=a_1+a_2=23/20,    M=2(b+S)=63/10.

In the reflected theorem the lower bound is Gamma_1 b+S, where Gamma_1=1/2. Its value here would be

    Gamma_1 b+S=43/20.                             (2)

Define UNNORMALIZED depth D_S(Y)=inf_{H containing Y} mu(H), over closed ambient halfspaces. We prove

    max_{Y in C intersect(Z times R)} D_S(Y)=17/8
        =43/20-1/40.                              (3)

Thus no relocated middle center, and in fact no mark anywhere in the mixed support, attains (2).

Each outer interval pair separately has a reflection center: -19/40 for the near pair and -19/20 for the far pair. There is no common reflection center. More substantively, (3) rules out any alternative measure-preserving allocation that would imply the same full credit without literal reflection.

## 2. Four actual caps cover all integer planes

Put y_*=-1/40. At base 0 consider

    H_0^+={x+1/40-z/4>=0},
    H_0^-={-x-1/40-2z>=0}.                         (4)

They pass through (0,y_*). Their fiber masses, in increasing base order, are respectively

    (0,13/40,41/40,31/40,0,0),
    (1/10,21/20,39/40,0,0,0).

Both total 17/8. The sum of their displayed margins is -9z/4. Therefore their union contains EVERY continuous point over every integer base z<=0. This statement does not require a bound on x or membership in C.

Reflect these two caps in the base coordinate z->1-z. Because C is invariant under this base reflection, the resulting caps H_1^+,H_1^- also have mass 17/8. Their margins sum to 9(z-1)/4, so their union contains every continuous point over z>=1. Together the four caps cover all integer planes globally. This proves the upper bound in (3), including every competing old or new candidate mark over the covered planes.

## 3. Exact all-normal lower certificate at the two actual marks

Every nonvertical through-(0,y_*) line has the form x=y_*+tz. Write

    F(t)=sum_{z=-2}^3 clamp(h_z-y_*-tz,0,h_z+1),    (5)

where h_z is the upper endpoint in (1). This is the mass of the upward halfspace. The downward halfspace has mass M-F(t): every nonvertical boundary meets each interval in a singleton of one-dimensional measure zero.

The function F is continuous and piecewise affine. Its complete finite knot list and values are

| t | F(t) | M-F(t) |
|---|---:|---:|
| -39/40 | 167/40 | 17/8 |
| -39/80 | 59/16 | 209/80 |
| -13/40 | 16/5 | 31/10 |
| -7/24 | 3 | 33/10 |
| -3/40 | 47/20 | 79/20 |
| 3/80 | 17/8 | 167/40 |
| 7/16 | 17/8 | 167/40 |
| 39/80 | 89/40 | 163/40 |
| 39/40 | 89/40 | 163/40 |
| 41/40 | 87/40 | 33/8 |

The two tails are constant: F=167/40 to the left and F=87/40 to the right. Hence

    min_t F(t)=17/8,     max_t F(t)=167/40=M-17/8.

Both orientations of every nonvertical through-point halfspace have mass at least17/8. Pure-base halfspaces through base0 have masses63/20 and103/20, also larger. Every containing halfspace contains a parallel through-point halfspace, completing the all-halfspace proof. Base reflection proves the identical lower bound at (1,y_*). Together with Section2 this proves (3).

As an earlier diagnostic, the original middle centroid (0,0) already fails (2): the cap x>=(2/5)z has fiber masses (0,9/20,1,3/5,0,0), total41/20. The optimized calculation above is essential: it excludes repairing that failure by shifting the common center.

## 4. What fails in the collective allocation

The reflected proof takes the kth missing interval and sends it into the positive scalar band (kt,(k+1)t) of the SAME other-middle cap. Distinct k give disjoint bands. Equal masses and containment in B do not supply this directional reflection. In (1), the near and far outer pairs place their mass near the same lower end; their different pair centers cannot share that disjoint-band allocation.

The strongest precise obstruction is numerical and independent of a chosen transport: ANY proposed common-center or measure-preserving pairing theorem implying Gamma_d|B|+sum a_k for all such equal-mass compatible pairs is false, since its conclusion contradicts the global four-cap certificate (4). This does not preclude smaller payments or a transport condition with additional directional structure.

The normalized value here is

    (17/8)/(63/10)=85/252>1/4.

The n=1,d=1 OC target is1/4, equivalently raw63/40. The example blocks the EXTRA full outer-pair credit43/20, not the conjectured centerpoint bound, nor a below-target variational argument.

## 5. Verification

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_asymmetric_paired_slabs_independent.py` uses exact rational arithmetic only. It checks compatibility, all listed knot values, both tails, the four cap budgets and covering margin sums, the original-centroid diagnostic, and the strict gap in (3). No floating optimizer is used in the certificate.
